In a 51-year-old man with an action tremor reproduced on finger-to-nose testing, intact cranial nerves II-XII help rule out significant neurological deficits.

A 51-year-old man has an action tremor that occurs during activities such as pouring drinks, pointing a remote, and working on his car, is reproduced with finger-to-nose testing, and is not present at rest.
Parkinson disease is less likely in this 51-year-old man with an action tremor because rigidity and bradykinesia are absent.

Essential tremor is a more probable diagnosis in this 51-year-old man with an action tremor during activities such as pouring drinks, pointing a remote, and working on his car, with tremor reproduced on finger-to-nose testing.
